title: Portland police respond to protests outside ICE facility - NewsBreak
text: PORTLAND, Ore. ( KOIN ) — About 60-70 protesters were seen outside the Portland Immigration and Customs Enforcement facility late Wednesday night. The gathering, which once again appeared to be setting up a barricade in front of the building, had grown in the past few hours. Around 10:45 p.m., the Portland Police Bureau said, via their PPB Event Messages X account, that they were about to make a “targeted arrest for a crime” amid the demonstrations. They announced on a sound truck a warning to other protesters not to interfere, on threat of being arrested. Earlier in the evening, PPB said they had been present during the demonstration but were not involved in any immigration enforcement. Around 7:20 p.m., Portland police said that officers observed federal law enforcement “deploy munitions as vehicles were exiting the ICE facility,” but PPB did not get involved at that point. Earlier in the afternoon, there were only about 20-30 people and the demonstrations remained peaceful during the majority of the day. Most people kept their distance from the front gate during the daytime gathering while protesters made their voices heard about the movement. This comes after a physical confrontation broke out between demonstrators and federal agents on Tuesday night. During that confrontation, federal agents fired rounds of pepper spray at protesters. KOIN 6 News crews saw some demonstrators creating a makeshift barricade out of a basketball hoop and large tables, appearing to block a vehicle entry point. Graffiti had also been painted on the building exterior. The response from federal agents included deploying flash-bangs and pepper balls. During a news conference on Wednesday, protesters made their stance clear: they want to get “ICE out of Portland,” as a message on one person’s sign read. “To those inside, we see you. We hear you. And we have not forgotten you,” the speaker said. KOIN 6 News reporter Ariel Iacobazzi attempted to ask the protester questions about the movement but the person replied, “I’m sorry, I’m just here to read this.” One woman who had participated in a daytime protest at the ICE facility but not during the nighttime altercations told KOIN 6 News, “I don’t agree with all of their tactics, but I understand we have the same goals and I absolutely support their efforts because of that.” During the Tuesday night protest, in which protesters were setting up barricades and federal agents were deploying pepper balls and flash-bangs, one man claims he got caught in the crossfire, displaying a wound on his legs. “It didn’t feel good, it felt pretty bad, it kind of hurt my feelings more than anything. I wasn’t doing anything to them,” the man said. Portland Police Bureau officers showed up just before midnight but did not make any arrests, though they said they worked to de-escalate the crowd and move them away from the ICE facility overnight on Tuesday. A smaller group of demonstrators returned and once again set up an encampment on the side of the building the following day. Earlier this week, Portland police also facilitated the posting of anti-camping signs, with a deadline posted for Friday afternoon. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to KOIN.com.
